display.purpose: Welcome headline in the empty Agent view only; uppercase.

title.purpose: Selected station name or Network at the head of the side panel; uppercase.

question.purpose: The user's question at the head of each turn; sentence case.

figure.purpose: Live run stats (22px) and network figures (26px), labelled underneath.

control.purpose: Nav items and buttons; uppercase; 13px on small buttons.

label.purpose: Terms, table headers, tags, badges, filters, line-ruled section headings; uppercase, 11.5 to 13px, 0.12 to 0.18em.

body.purpose: All prose, chips, inputs, table cells; tabular figures.

shadows.name: focus-ring
shadows.purpose: Text field keyboard focus, paired with a cobalt border.

shadows.name: ready-halo
shadows.purpose: Status lamp when the semantic index is ready.

shadows.name: station-pulse
shadows.purpose: Animated ring on the active route station (1.4s, infinite).

shadows.name: focus-outline
shadows.purpose: Global :focus-visible outline for every interactive element.

motion.name: ease
motion.purpose: System ease for arrivals, presses and pulses.

motion.name: state
motion.purpose: Colour, border and background transitions on hover.

motion.name: arrive
motion.purpose: New route stations and the answer panel entering.

motion.name: pulse
motion.purpose: Active station dot, and the map ring around the entity being read (grows 16px).

motion.name: route-grow
motion.purpose: Each route leg and its spurs drawing in on the map.

motion.name: ping
motion.purpose: Amber ring around an entity after a chip hover or click.

motion.name: reduced-motion

components.css: .ds-route{list-style:none;margin:0;padding:0;width:380px;color:var(--porcelain, #f4f1ea);font:15px/1.5 'Barlow', system-ui, sans-serif;} .ds-route li{position:relative;display:grid;grid-template-columns:34px 1fr;column-gap:14px;padding-bottom:18px;} .ds-route li::before{content:'';position:absolute;left:16px;top:22px;bottom:-2px;width:3px;background:var(--hairline-strong, rgba(244,241,234,0.5));} .ds-route li:last-child::before{display:none;} .ds-route li.done::before{background:var(--porcelain, #f4f1ea);} .ds-route .dot{position:relative;z-index:1;width:34px;height:34px;border-radius:50%;display:grid;place-items:center;background:var(--enamel, #0b1230);border:3px solid var(--hairline-strong, rgba(244,241,234,0.5));font:700 13px/1 'Barlow Condensed', 'Arial Narrow', sans-serif;color:var(--ink-2, #bcc4de);} .ds-route .done .dot,.ds-route .active .dot{border-color:var(--porcelain, #f4f1ea);color:var(--porcelain, #f4f1ea);} .ds-route .active .dot{animation:ds-pulse 1.4s cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1) infinite;} .ds-route h3{display:flex;gap:10px;align-items:baseline;margin:5px 0 0;font:600 16px/1.25 'Barlow Condensed', 'Arial Narrow', sans-serif;letter-spacing:0.1em;text-transform:uppercase;} .ds-route h3 span{font:400 15px 'Barlow', system-ui, sans-serif;letter-spacing:0;text-transform:none;color:var(--ink-2, #bcc4de);} .ds-route h3 em{font:600 13px 'Barlow Condensed', 'Arial Narrow', sans-serif;font-style:normal;letter-spacing:0.06em;color:var(--amber, #ffc20e);} .ds-route p{margin:4px 0 0;font-size:14.5px;color:var(--ink-2, #bcc4de);} @keyframes ds-pulse{0%{box-shadow:0 0 0 0 rgba(244,241,234,0.55);}100%{box-shadow:0 0 0 12px rgba(244,241,234,0);}} @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce){.ds-route .active .dot{animation:none;}}

narrative.overview:
Nexus is drawn as a city transit system at night. The ground is deep midnight enamel, text is warm porcelain, and each entity type runs on its own line ink, the way a metro map gives every line one colour. The agent's reasoning is a journey: every thinking summary and tool call arrives as a numbered station on a vertical route line, and every entity it reads lights up on the map in order. The whole network stays readable like a transit map rather than a glowing hairball. Once a route exists, only the route burns bright and everything else fades back.

The density is operational. A fixed left rail holds the brand, view switcher and a live status board. Content runs in tall columns divided by hairlines: the journey column and the map in Agent, the map and a station card in Graph, a reading page in MCP. Type speaks in two registers. Condensed, tracked transit capitals (Barlow Condensed) handle every heading, label, control and figure. Plain Barlow handles prose and data values, with tabular figures throughout. Depth comes from layered enamel tones and porcelain hairlines, never from blurred shadows.

The world rejects the usual "AI dashboard" look: no neon glow graph, no chat drawer, no glassy floating cards. It reads like printed enamel signage that happens to move.
keyCharacteristics: Midnight enamel ground in four tonal strata; porcelain ink in three strengths.
One line ink per entity type, reused everywhere that type appears (dash marker, station ring, link tint, badge).
Condensed uppercase transit capitals with wide tracking for every label and control.
Hairline-ruled panels and gently squared corners (2 to 4px); circles are reserved for stations, lamps and dots.
The signature: the agent's route drawn on the map as a cased porcelain line, station by station, numbered, with the rest of the network dimmed.

rules.name: The One Line, One Ink Rule
rules.body: Each entity type owns exactly one ink (services cobalt, teams amber, people scarlet, standards green, tools violet, guides teal). Wherever that type appears (the 18 by 4px line dash, a station ring, a link tint, a type badge, a filter button), it uses that ink and no other.

rules.name: The Scarlet Departure Rule
rules.body: A scarlet fill is reserved for the single primary action in a view. Everywhere else, scarlet appears only as a thin signal: a 3px underline, a 7px dot or a caret.

rules.name: The Ink Stays Porcelain Rule
rules.body: Prose and headings are set only in porcelain, mist or dusk ink. Line inks never set running text. The one exception is amber, for short status words and timings.

rules.name: The Transit Capitals Rule
rules.body: Every heading, label, control and figure is set in Barlow Condensed. Labels and controls are uppercase and tracked between 0.1em and 0.18em. Prose, questions and data values stay in Barlow, sentence case.

rules.name: The Tabular Figures Rule
rules.body: Tabular numerals are on from the body down, so timings, counts and stats never jitter while they tick.

rules.name: The Enamel Strata Rule
rules.body: To lift something, move it one enamel stratum and give it a hairline. Never add a blur shadow or a glow.

rules.name: The Gently Squared Rule
rules.body: Rectangles never go above 4px radius and are never pills. A circle always means a station or a signal.

rules.name: The Route Burns Rule
rules.body: Once a route exists, every station off it drops to 14% opacity and every link off it to 5%. The route is the only bright thing on the map. Graph selection follows the same rule: the selected station's neighbourhood stays lit and everything else dims.

rules.name: The Legible Map Rule
rules.body: Labels are placed in priority order (current station, then stamp order, then interchanges, then the rest) and dropped rather than overlapped.

dos: **Do** take every entity colour from its line ink (cobalt, amber, scarlet, green, violet, teal) and use that same ink everywhere the type appears.
**Do** set every label, heading and control in Barlow Condensed uppercase with 0.1 to 0.18em tracking, and every sentence in Barlow.
**Do** build depth from the four enamel strata plus 1px porcelain hairlines (24% or 50%).
**Do** keep rectangles at 2px (badges), 3px (chips) or 4px (controls and panels), and reserve circles for stations and signals.
**Do** inset bars, panels and map overlays by the 22px gutter, and drop to 16px at 960px and below.
**Do** use the system ease `cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)` for arrivals and presses, 0.2s for colour changes, and disable all animation under `prefers-reduced-motion`.
**Do** dim everything off the route (stations 14%, links 5%) once the agent starts travelling.
donts: **Don't** use blurred drop shadows or glows. The only box-shadows are zero-blur spread rings for focus, the ready lamp and the station pulse.
**Don't** draw the network as a neon hairball. Off-route links stay faint and labels never overlap.
**Don't** fill more than one action per view with scarlet, or use a line ink for running text (amber status words excepted).
**Don't** set white ink on a badge fill that cannot hold 4.5:1 at 11.5px. Use the enamel-ink variant instead.
**Don't** introduce pill shapes, radii above 4px or a third typeface.
**Don't** stack a small caps label above a display headline. Section labels are themselves headings, ruled out with a trailing hairline.
